definition: Google Goggles was an image recognition mobile app developed by Google.
details: It was used for searches based on pictures taken by handheld devices. For example, taking a picture of a famous landmark searches for information about it, or taking a picture of a product's barcode would search for information on the product.

explainer.lead: Google Goggles was a mobile app that let people search with a photograph instead of typed words. It made image recognition useful for everyday tasks such as learning about a landmark or looking up a product from its barcode.

tiers.eli5: Imagine showing a librarian a photo instead of trying to describe what you see. Google Goggles let a handheld device do something similar: you could photograph a famous landmark to find information about it, or scan a product's barcode to look up the product.
tiers.practitioner: Treat it as a visual-search client: the input is a photo from a handheld device, and the output is search information about the pictured subject. The integration points are image capture and search rather than a standalone product or landmark database. Its described uses target recognizable landmarks and product barcodes, not identification of every possible object.
tiers.paperLevel: Google Goggles implements image-based retrieval: given an image I captured by a handheld device, form a search request q(I) and return information R(q(I)) about the depicted entity. The demonstrated mappings include landmark image -> landmark information and product barcode -> product information. It is an application-level visual-search system, not a specified recognition model or benchmark.

explainer.example: A traveler photographs a famous landmark instead of typing its description. Google Goggles uses that picture to search for information about the landmark.

usedIn.name: Landmark information search
usedIn.detail: A photo of a famous landmark is used to search for information about that landmark.

usedIn.name: Product lookup
usedIn.detail: A photo of a product's barcode is used to search for information about the product.

explainer.intuition: A picture can sometimes express a search better than words. Goggles used the contents of a photo as the starting point for finding information.
howItWorks: A person takes a picture with a handheld device.
The app uses image recognition to interpret the pictured subject.
The picture becomes the basis of a search.
The app returns information about the landmark or product.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connected phone cameras with search, offering a direct way to ask about something visible even when its name was unknown.
misconceptions: It was a mobile app, not a wearable device.
A photo was the search input; it did not replace all text searches.
Its described examples concern landmarks and barcodes, not recognition of every object.
